thread_analysis.thread_summary: Topre Corporation (contacts Kenki Enomoto, Seiji Hiraki) engages Allion (Itsuo Sakai, Toshitaka Mochizuki, Masaya Iida, Kentaro Taniguchi, Misumi Sato) across two related engagements for the same RC1-series keyboard product line (cross-referenced with thread_0001), spanning May 2024 through March 2025: an initial combined WHQL+Bluetooth SIG dual-certification project, followed by a series of post-registration scoping questions (module manufacturer transitions, Core Specification version upgrades, key-code additions), and finally a distinct OEM/brand-owner registration for PFU (a different brand, with Topre manufacturing on PFU's behalf), which surfaced significant registration-identity and credential-handling complexity.
all_questions_found: Does a referenced module's manufacturer transition (Taiyo Yuden to Kaga FEI) require any registration update, given the QDID itself doesn't change? (see thread_0026_case_01)

Can an existing registration's declared Bluetooth Core Specification version be upgraded (e.g., 4.2 to 5.0) without new testing, given the referenced QDID is actually higher-spec? (see thread_0026_case_02)
Does adding a new HID key code (a Mute key) to an already-certified keyboard require re-application? (see thread_0026_case_03)

Whose login credentials (Username/Password) should be used for an OEM registration filed under a different brand owner's name, and what if that brand owner won't disclose their credentials? (see thread_0026_case_04)

(Internal quality control) Was the Invoice used for Qualification Fee payment obtained under the correct company's account, given the registrant is the brand owner (PFU) rather than the manufacturer (Topre) handling logistics? (see thread_0026_case_05)

(Administrative, not separately cased) WHQL+Bluetooth dual-certification project setup and test sequencing (Bluetooth before USB before WHQL), free derivative registration of JP/US keyboard variants from one representative tested model, standard Compliance Folder document checklist, and registration completion/Review Page confirmation logistics -- consistent with administrative content already documented in other threads.
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: This thread is notable for documenting two previously undocumented but highly specific and consequential rules: the Core Specification version lock-in at registration time (case_02), which directly contradicts a naive assumption that a registration's declared spec simply mirrors whatever the referenced component currently supports; and the QDID Listing-Owner-transition exemption (case_01), which clarifies when a downstream registration is and isn't affected by an upstream component manufacturer change. Case_04 and case_05 together document a complete, realistic OEM/brand-owner registration-identity scenario, including a practical workaround for credential-disclosure refusal and an internal safeguard against a near-miss payment-account mismatch.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: See thread_0026_case_01 through thread_0026_case_05 for case-specific decision logic.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: See individual case files; case_02 carries the most consequential risk of customer misunderstanding (assuming a spec upgrade is a simple edit rather than a new registration), while case_05 documents a real near-miss that could have caused a payment/registration mismatch if not caught internally before the wire transfer was finalized.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: Case_05 documents a genuine internal near-miss: an Invoice obtained under the wrong company's account (the manufacturer's rather than the brand owner's) was initially queued for wire-transfer payment before being caught and corrected -- an explicit, valuable example of the kind of cross-check needed in OEM/brand-owner scenarios where registrant identity and the company handling logistics differ.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a registration's declared Core Specification version doesn't match what the customer expects (e.g., due to a deliberate downgrade at original registration time), explain the system's spec-version lock-in clearly rather than letting the customer assume a simple edit is possible; and in OEM/brand-owner registration scenarios, explicitly verify both the login credential identity AND the payment Invoice's account ownership against the actual registrant (the brand owner), since these can be independently gotten wrong even after the registrant-identity question itself has been correctly resolved.
